newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar closes stronger in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar closes stronger in thin trading.

text.p: * The Canadian dollar closed firmer on Monday at C$1.3616 (US$0.7345) from Friday's close at C$1.3641 (US$0.7331) in quiet trading, dealers said. * The currency strengthened after Standard and Poor's upgraded Canada's foreign currency debt rating outlook. * Unit also aided by statistics showing foreigners bought more Canadian securities in December
But the debt rating agency said Canada still has too much debt to be reassigned the top triple-A rating it lost in 1992.
Statistics showing foreigners bought more Canadian securities in December also helped the Canada dollar, dealers said.
Foreign investors bought a net C$3.29 billion of Canadian securities in December after selling a net C$3.52 billion in November, Statistics Canada said on Monday.
For all of 1996, foreign investors bought a net C$18.91 billion of Canadian securities, down from C$22.15 billion in 1995, the government agency said.
"It was a little bit of a surprise," said Michael Gregory, strategist for Lehman Brothers in Toronto.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar slid to 1.2280 marks from Friday's close at 1.2380 marks and fell to 89.67 yen from Friday's 90.23 yen.
